seo.title: Busy Barbershop, Low Profit? Measure Earnings per Chair-Hour
seo.description: A full diary isn't the same as a profitable one. How UK barbershop owners can work out what each chair-hour earns, by service, and what to change.

media.anchor: # Your Diary Is Full. So Why Isn't Your Barbershop Making More Money?

media.anchor: The most expensive service isn't the most valuable use of the chair.

media.anchor: Day A takes £246 and produces £231.01 of contribution
media.alt: Two hypothetical equally busy eight-hour barber-chair days compared: Day A £246 revenue and £231.01 contribution, Day B £274 revenue and £256.79 contribution, both 475 of 480 minutes booked
media.caption: Equal diary utilisation can produce different contribution: £25.78 extra for Day B in this hypothetical illustration; fixed overheads are not deducted
